newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia to look at improving public debt profile.
newsitem.headline: Colombia to look at improving public debt profile.

text.p: Colombia will set up a debt management committee to assess its $16 billion public sector debt, a senior official at the Finance Ministry said Monday.
The committee will include Finance Ministry and central bank representatives and is due to begin work before the end of April, said Clemente del Valle, head of public credit at the Finance Ministry.

"The work of the committee will not amount to a restructing of the public sector debt. The aim is to look at ways of improving our debt profile by looking at the average period of credit, interest rates and the denomination of foreign debt," Del Valle told Reuters.
The committee will make recommendations on changing foreign debt from one currency denomination to another, or on switching from fixed to floating interest rates.

Del Valle said one of the first tasks of the committee would be to look at swapping yen-denominated debt for more dollar-denominated debt. Colombia may issue new foreign debt during 1997, but did not give any indication as to how much.
It is estimated Colombia pays $2.5 billion a year in foreign debt servicing, $1.5 billion of which is disbursed by the central government.
